entries.cuda_mechanism: cudaMalloc + cudaMemcpy H2D/D2H around every kernel
entries.why_it_exists: a discrete GPU has its own physical memory the CPU cannot address
entries.underlying_problem: data must physically cross PCIe to be computed on
entries.apple_equivalent: none needed; CPU and GPU address the same physical memory
entries.hawking_equivalent: operands stay resident; no copy is issued at all

performance_gap.value: per-call copying costs 7.17-7.44x on a fused elementwise op, reproducible to 3.74% across 3 runs

entries.test_corpus: fused mul->relu->silu, 2^24 f32, resident vs copied
entries.remaining_limitation: the comparison uses the NAIVE CUDA pattern; a competent CUDA programmer hoists the upload and does not pay this

entries.cuda_mechanism: dequantize to dense then call cuBLAS, or a fused dequant-GEMM kernel
entries.why_it_exists: tensor cores consume dense formats; compact formats must be expanded
entries.underlying_problem: compact weights are not directly consumable by library GEMM
entries.apple_equivalent: none provided; MLX quantized ops cover its own formats only
entries.hawking_equivalent: representation-native matvec reading packed nibbles + f16 group scales

performance_gap.value: no advantage below ~64 MiB; 2.08x at 256 MiB where it becomes bandwidth-bound

entries.test_corpus: real Qwen3-30B-A3B expert tensor at ws_rtn_q4_g64
entries.current_winner: Hawking native kernel above the crossover; nothing below it
entries.remaining_limitation: matvec only; no GEMM, no batched form, and one expert sits BELOW the crossover so single-expert use gains nothing

entries.cuda_mechanism: hand-fused kernels, or a compiler like Triton/torch.compile
entries.why_it_exists: each launch re-reads and re-writes memory an op chain need not touch
entries.underlying_problem: unfused chains are bandwidth-bound on intermediates
entries.apple_equivalent: MLX does not fuse an arbitrary elementwise chain automatically
entries.hawking_equivalent: AIR lowers a multi-op SSA chain into one kernel

performance_gap.value: 1.71x over the naive 3-kernel translation, 2.62x over MLX

entries.remaining_limitation: elementwise chains over one shape and dtype only

entries.cuda_mechanism: NVRTC / driver JIT of PTX at runtime
entries.why_it_exists: shapes and constants are not known until run time
entries.underlying_problem: AOT compilation cannot specialise on runtime values
entries.apple_equivalent: Metal runtime library compilation; MLX exposes it via metal_kernel
entries.hawking_equivalent: AIR emits MSL, MLX JIT-compiles it

performance_gap.reason: compile latency has not been measured

entries.test_corpus: the six AIR programs of P3
entries.current_winner: MLX JIT (retained; nothing here replaces it)
entries.remaining_limitation: xcrun metal is ABSENT on this machine, so AOT metallib compilation is unavailable and there is no offline compile path at all

entries.cuda_mechanism: template parameters and __constant__ values baked at compile time
entries.why_it_exists: a constant known at compile time removes a load and enables unrolling
entries.hawking_equivalent: AirProgram.specialization emits const floats into the MSL

performance_gap.reason: specialisation was never isolated as its own arm

entries.test_corpus: saxpy->relu with ALPHA as a specialization constant
entries.current_winner: UNKNOWN — never measured against a non-specialised variant
entries.remaining_limitation: scalar floats only; no types, no shapes, no predicates

entries.why_it_exists: a portable way to index a data-parallel launch
entries.underlying_problem: mapping work onto a hierarchy of parallel units
entries.hawking_equivalent: C2M recognises the canonical global index and maps it
entries.test_corpus: the four translated kernels of P4
entries.current_winner: Hawking C2M for the canonical form
entries.remaining_limitation: ONLY the 1-D canonical form; no 2-D or 3-D grids, no block-relative indexing, no grid-stride loops

entries.why_it_exists: a software-managed scratchpad far faster than global memory
entries.underlying_problem: reuse within a block should not go to DRAM

performance_gap.value: MLX 12733 GFLOP/s vs ours 2683 at 2048^2 = 4.7x in MLX's favour

entries.test_corpus: 512/1024/2048 square f32 GEMM vs MLX, plus 2 negative controls
entries.current_winner: MLX, retained (§141) -- replacement is not justified by evidence
entries.remaining_limitation: threadgroup tiles execute; no double buffering, no bank-conflict work

entries.cuda_mechanism: atomicAdd/atomicCAS on global and shared memory
entries.why_it_exists: concurrent accumulation without a separate reduction pass
entries.remaining_limitation: blocks histogram, scatter, and any single-pass reduction

entries.why_it_exists: intra-warp exchange without shared memory or barriers
entries.underlying_problem: lane-to-lane communication inside a scheduling unit
entries.apple_equivalent: simd_shuffle and friends over a 32-wide SIMD group
entries.hawking_equivalent: simdgroup_float8x8 matrix ops in AIR's simdgroup matmul strategy

performance_gap.value: 1.6x over a scalar tile; 91-98% of MLX at 512/1024 but 36.7% at 2048

entries.test_corpus: 512/1024/2048 f32 GEMM, simdgroup vs tiled vs MLX
entries.remaining_limitation: simdgroup MATRIX ops work; shuffle, ballot and vote are still untouched, and Apple's divergence semantics remain uncompared to CUDA's

performance_gap.value: MLX 12733 GFLOP/s vs ours 2683 at 2048^2 = 4.7x in MLX's favour

entries.test_corpus: 512/1024/2048 square f32 GEMM vs MLX, plus 2 negative controls
entries.current_winner: MLX, retained (§141) -- replacement is not justified by evidence
entries.remaining_limitation: threadgroup_barrier executes; SIMDGROUP and DEVICE scope untested, and AIR can represent a barrier but cannot lower one

entries.why_it_exists: matrix multiply is the dominant cost of a transformer
entries.underlying_problem: peak arithmetic needs tiling, blocking and hardware MMA units
entries.apple_equivalent: MLX matmul; Apple matrix coprocessor via MPS

performance_gap.value: best AIR strategy reaches 36.7% of MLX at 2048

entries.test_corpus: 512/1024/2048 square f32 GEMM vs MLX, plus 2 negative controls
entries.current_winner: MLX, retained (§141) -- replacement is not justified by evidence
entries.remaining_limitation: no hierarchical blocking -- one 8x8 tile per simdgroup streaming operands from device memory, which is why it collapses to 36.7% of MLX at 2048 while holding 91-98% at 1024 and below

entries.why_it_exists: reductions are latency-critical and hard to write well
entries.underlying_problem: tree reduction across a hierarchy with correct synchronization
entries.remaining_limitation: softmax and normalization both need this, so attention is blocked behind it

entries.cuda_mechanism: cudaStream_t, cudaEvent_t, async launch and dependency ordering
entries.why_it_exists: overlap of compute and transfer, and explicit dependency expression
entries.underlying_problem: serialising independent work wastes the device
entries.hawking_equivalent: NONE; AIR expresses dependencies as SSA but not asynchrony
entries.remaining_limitation: C2M-T1 explicitly requires this and is NOT claimed

entries.cuda_mechanism: CUDA Graphs: capture once, replay with minimal launch overhead
entries.why_it_exists: per-launch CPU cost dominates short kernels in a tight loop
entries.underlying_problem: re-encoding an unchanged command stream every iteration
entries.apple_equivalent: indirect command buffers; reusable command buffers

performance_gap.reason: launch overhead has not been isolated, though the P7 crossover shows small ops ARE launch-bound here

entries.remaining_limitation: the decode loop is exactly the shape this targets, and the evidence that small kernels are launch-bound is already in the P7 sweep

entries.underlying_problem: attributing time to a specific kernel on an async device
entries.hawking_equivalent: bench.py wall-clock with warmup, IQR gate and an implausibility rejection

performance_gap.reason: the instrument is not itself benchmarked

entries.test_corpus: every timed arm in P5, P6, P7
entries.remaining_limitation: WALL CLOCK ONLY — no DRAM byte counters, no occupancy, no stall reasons, so mechanism is inferred rather than observed

entries.why_it_exists: silent numerical corruption is the worst failure mode
entries.underlying_problem: a wrong answer at speed looks like a right answer
entries.apple_equivalent: Metal shader validation, GPU frame capture
entries.hawking_equivalent: every candidate verified against an oracle BEFORE it is timed
entries.test_corpus: P3 six programs, P4 four kernels, forge 15 variants
entries.remaining_limitation: oracle comparison only; no race detection, no OOB checking, no device-side assertion

entries.why_it_exists: multi-GPU training and inference need direct device-to-device paths
entries.underlying_problem: moving tensors between devices without a host bounce
entries.apple_equivalent: none on a single SoC; Thunderbolt/RDMA between machines
entries.hawking_equivalent: HUMF models the domains but only a MOCK external one exists

performance_gap.reason: no real second device exists; every transport number so far is SIMULATED and may not be cited as evidence

entries.test_corpus: HUMF P8 across APPLE_UM and MOCK_EXTERNAL_VRAM
entries.current_winner: NOT APPLICABLE — no second physical device
entries.remaining_limitation: EGB-D0 has not been reached; no hardware is present

parity_claim: NOT CLAIMED. This is a capability inventory, not a parity statement. No entry may report a semantic gap of NONE without evidence, and the steer forbids the phrase 'CUDA parity' unqualified.
coverage_honesty: The CUDA surface is vastly larger than this. These are the capabilities reachable or relevant from what has actually been built here; absence from this ledger means NOT YET STUDIED, never NOT NEEDED.
